paragraphs: A student of Rava. [Mentioned in] Bava Batra 139a, [where he] sent to Rava [the request], "Let our master teach us."[^1][^2]

notes.text: An isolated כ precedes the citation in the frozen text; the clear student-and-letter statement is translated without inventing an expansion.

The subject of sent is supplied contextually from the heading; Hyman calls him Rava’s student and has him send to Rava, in that direction. רבינו is our master as a direct honorific, not a separately inferred personal rank; Rava remains a name. Isolated כ remains in Hebrew without a certain expanded word, and139a follows the period convention without named-edition verification.
